key_insight: Post-sampling symbolic constraints can turn a statistically plausible trajectory generator into a structurally admissible one, especially as graph complexity rises.
engineering_relevance: For dynamic graph systems, combining diffusion-based generation with constraint checking/repair improves the reliability of predicted trajectories for planning and decision support.
method: Conditional diffusion generates future graph-state trajectories from partial observations.
An external symbolic layer enforces constraints via hard filtering, soft weighting, or projection-based repair.
Performance is compared across two synthetic graph regimes using validity, sample efficiency, diversity, robustness, and calibration metrics.
evidence_signal: Invalid probability mass was very low in the compact graph (0.002996) but much higher in the medium-complexity graph (0.155929); hard filtering eliminated invalid retained trajectories while keeping 84.4% of generated samples.
watch_item: Constraint handling may improve admissibility, but hard filtering can reduce retained sample diversity and the approach was validated only on controlled synthetic regimes.
paper_title: Bridging the Gap Between Plausibility and Admissibility: Constraint-Aware Flow Maps for Dynamic Graph Systems
